quiz.title: Implicit Differentiation Quiz (Exercise 5.3)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on finding dy/dx for implicit relations, exactly the skills NCERT Exercise 5.3 tests. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Maths Exercise 5.3 — implicit differentiation

questions.q: For x² + y² = 1, what is dy/dx?
questions.explanation: Differentiate term by term: 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0. Solving gives dy/dx = −x/y.

questions.q: The core idea of implicit differentiation is that y is treated as
options: a function of x, so d/dx of yⁿ needs the chain rule
questions.explanation: Since y depends on x, differentiating any term in y brings out a factor of dy/dx by the chain rule — for example d/dx(y²) = 2y·(dy/dx).

questions.q: For 2x + 3y = sin x, what is dy/dx?
questions.explanation: Differentiate: 2 + 3(dy/dx) = cos x. So 3(dy/dx) = cos x − 2, giving dy/dx = (cos x − 2)/3.

questions.q: Differentiating the product term xy with respect to x gives
questions.explanation: Use the product rule: d/dx(xy) = x(dy/dx) + y·1 = y + x(dy/dx). This step trips up many students in Exercise 5.3.

questions.q: For x² + xy + y² = 100, dy/dx equals
questions.explanation: Differentiate: 2x + (y + x·dy/dx) + 2y(dy/dx) = 0. Group dy/dx: (x + 2y)dy/dx = −(2x + y), so dy/dx = −(2x + y)/(x + 2y).

questions.q: If y = sin⁻¹x, then dy/dx is
questions.explanation: The inverse-trig relation sin y = x differentiates to cos y·(dy/dx) = 1. Since cos y = √(1 − x²), dy/dx = 1/√(1 − x²).
From tan y = x, sec²y·(dy/dx) = 1. Since sec²y = 1 + tan²y = 1 + x², dy/dx = 1/(1 + x²).

questions.q: For sin²y + cos(xy) = k, the derivative of cos(xy) with respect to x is
questions.explanation: Chain rule on cos(u) with u = xy: d/dx cos(xy) = −sin(xy)·d/dx(xy) = −sin(xy)·(y + x·dy/dx).

faq.q: What does Exercise 5.3 of NCERT Class 12 Maths cover?
faq.a: Exercise 5.3 is about implicit differentiation — finding dy/dx when x and y are tied together in one equation, such as x² + y² = 1 or ax + by² = cos y, rather than y written explicitly as a function of x.

faq.q: How is implicit differentiation different from Exercise 5.2?
faq.a: Exercise 5.2 applies the chain rule to explicit functions like y = sin(x²). In 5.3 y is never isolated, so every y-term picks up a dy/dx factor and you solve algebraically for dy/dx at the end.

faq.q: Why does a dy/dx term appear when I differentiate y² or xy?
faq.a: Because y is itself a function of x. By the chain rule d/dx(y²) = 2y·(dy/dx), and by the product rule d/dx(xy) = y + x·(dy/dx). Forgetting this factor is the most common Exercise 5.3 mistake.

faq.q: Do inverse trigonometric functions appear in this exercise?
faq.a: Yes. Several questions use relations like y = sin⁻¹x or tan y = x. You differentiate the trig form implicitly and substitute back to get standard results such as 1/√(1 − x²) or 1/(1 + x²).
